newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Solid Energy six month net profit NZ$7.67 mln.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Solid Energy six month net profit NZ$7.67 mln.

text.p: Solid Energy New Zealand Ltd (previously known as Coal Corp of NZ), on Thursday reported a six month after tax profit of NZ$7.67 million, compared to more than $9 million for the previous corresponding period.
The company said it had a challenging and busy six months ahead of it, and the half year results showed it was on track for continued growth.
Chief executive Ian Collinson said the half year figures reflected a continued pattern of steady growth for the business, although the strength of the New Zealand dollar had an impact.
"The strong dollar is something all exporters are having to deal with and in our case it has reduced the net profit by around 22 percent relative to last year," he said.
"However, a 12 percent increase in sales turnover and a similar increase in sales volume are good signs for the company."
He said Solid Energy's export volume was up 8.6 percent on the previous comparable half year, and productivity rose seven percent to 2,203 tonnes of coal sold per employee.
At the same time, the company had made considerable investments in mine development and exporation, fixed assets and the feasibility study into the West Coast export jetty.

The company's main capital expenditure in the period was for the installation of a new blending plant at its Rotowaro mine near Huntly, a new screening and coal bagging plant at Ohai and the ongoing development of the Mount Davy mine on the West Coast.
